newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG-Caltex cuts petrol price to lowest in S.Korea.
newsitem.headline: LG-Caltex cuts petrol price to lowest in S.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's LG-Caltex Oil Corp said on Friday it has lowered its retail petrol prices to 825 won per litre from 833 won -- the lowest level offered by the country's refiners.
"Our ultimate goal is to win additional market share," said a company spokesman.
LG-Caltex holds the second largest share of domestic petrol market at 31.7 percent, following Yukong Ltd's 37.5 percent, analysts said
"We also want to remove a set image as a company that sells the most expensive petrol," the spokesman said.
LG-Caltex and Yukong have offered the highest retail pump prices in South Korea among the refining sector since domestic prices were deregulated on January 1.
LG-Caltex's previous price of 833 won was higher than the 828 won currently offered by Ssangyong Oil Refining Co and Hyundai Oil Refinery Co, and the 827 won offered by Hanwha Energy Co Ltd.
Refiners raised petrol prices in the two months following deregulation. But with crude oil prices falling, they have started cutting prices.
